name: TouchView
summary: A large virtual panel within arm's reach follows the head and shows a zoomable view of the scene; the user selects a distant object by poking its magnified image on the panel with the index finger.
howItWorks: The panel covers the whole view and moves with the head, so it never needs placing. A pinch with either hand, moved up or down, zooms the view on the panel; turning the palm towards the face resets it. When the fingertip passes through the panel, a ray is cast from the view origin through the touched point and selects what it hits. It adapts ViewfinderVR so that view shifts need no panel manipulation. In a multi-target selection study with 23 participants on a Quest, it gave shorter movement times, lower workload and higher preference than Meta's freehand Hybrid Ray at all target sizes.
advantages: Direct touch on magnified proxies of distant objects.
Works with frequent view shifts without repositioning a panel.
limitations: Designed and tested for planar UI panels, not cluttered 3D scenes at varied depths.
Mid-air touch depends on hand-tracking quality.

relationships.note: Same authors; the panel now follows the head and zooms with a pinch.
